subject: Aurora Health — PHI handling technical questionnaire and BAA next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Lin <rachel.lin@aurorahealth.org>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evan Cho <evan.cho@aurorahealth.org>, legal@aurorahealth.org
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora Health PHI questionnaire for Redwood

Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking part in our RFP. Attached is the specific PHI/technical questionnaire we use to validate vendor readiness for sensitive healthcare workloads. Can you please: 

- Confirm the data flow for PHI when using Redwood hosted inference (what hits your control plane vs. customer infrastructure).
- Describe encryption in transit and at rest, including algorithms and key management options (customer-managed keys?).
- State default data retention and how deletion on demand is handled for inference logs and KV cache.
- Explain audit logging: what events include PHI, how long logs are retained, and whether logs can be restricted to metadata-only.
- Provide your subprocessor list and approach to notifying customers of changes.
- Confirm whether Redwood offers a private (VPC/on-prem) deployment option that avoids sending PHI to a shared control plane.
- Attach SOC 2 or other relevant certifications and any sample BAA text you propose.

We need your responses and any evidence for our security team by end of week (5 business days). If you prefer, we can book a short call to go through details.

Attached: Aurora_RFP_PHI_Qs.xlsx (our questionnaire).

Best,
Rachel Lin
Senior Procurement Manager
Aurora Health
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Lin <rachel.lin@aurorahealth.org>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora Health PHI questionnaire for Redwood

Hi Rachel — thanks for the questionnaire. We can meet your 5-business-day window and have started to assemble the technical packet. High-level answers below; attached is a preliminary packet and a redline-friendly BAA. We'll follow up with a short call to walk through any items your security/legal team wants to deep-dive.

High-level summary (hosted API):
- Data flow: Customer request (prompt + metadata) flows to the Redwood serving runtime in the selected region. The control plane coordinates routing and model selection; customer payloads are not retained in the control plane beyond active inference processing unless caching is explicitly enabled. Prefix/KV cache is configurable and can be disabled.
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 for in-transit; AES-256-GCM at rest. We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / GCP CMEK integrations for hosted Dedicated customers and for Private deployments.
- Retention & deletion: Default inference logs and telemetry are retained for 30 days; customers can request immediate deletion via API or opt into shorter retention. Cache entries are evictable and deletable on-demand.
- Audit logs: We provide configurable audit logging. By default logs capture request metadata and routing events; inclusion of full-text request/response is opt-in and can be scoped per-route. Logs are available via secure export or retained in customer-owned buckets in Private deployments.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a small list of cloud infra partners and telemetry providers; we supply an up-to-date subprocessor list and notify customers 30 days before material changes.
- Private / On‑prem: Redwood Private (VPC and on‑prem options) keeps inference in a customer-managed network; control plane can be offered as a private instance for regulated environments.

Attached: Redwood_BAA_redline_v1.pdf, redwood_data_flow_diagram.png, SOC2_certificate_2025.pdf

Proposed next steps:
1) Monica (cc'd) will provide the technical evidence and a detailed dataflow artifact.
2) Can we schedule a 45-minute walkthrough on Thu or Fri (I have availability Thu 10–11 PT)?

Thanks — looking forward to working through the questionnaire.

Regards,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Healthcare GTM
Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Lin <rachel.lin@aurorahealth.org>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evan Cho <evan.cho@aurorahealth.org>, legal@aurorahealth.org
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora Health PHI questionnaire for Redwood

Ava — thanks for the quick summary and the packet. A couple of clarifying questions from our security/legal teams before we set the call:

- Retention: you note 30 days default. Can the customer set a shorter system-wide retention (e.g., 7 days)? Is there an API for purge-by-customer and a certificate that purge completed?
- Logs: When audit logging is set to include full text, are logs encrypted with the same KMS keys or separate keys? Will logs ever be accessible by Redwood support if customer-managed keys are used?
- Subprocessors: can you share the current subprocessor list or a link? We need to confirm any subprocessors that may access PHI.
- BAA: Your redline looked reasonable; legal asked whether Redwood accepts a mutual indemnity clause and whether you can remove the 'broad liability carveouts' clause on page 4 (see attached legal checklist).
- Private deployment: we want to confirm there is an on‑prem option for fully air-gapped inference and whether the control plane is required to be reachable for licensing checks.

Thanks — if you can answer these in writing prior to the call it will speed review.

Rachel
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Lin <rachel.lin@aurorahealth.org>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora Health PHI questionnaire for Redwood

Hi Rachel — Monica from Solutions Engineering here. Quick technical replies to your clarifiers: 

- Retention/purge: Yes — customers can set retention per-organization or per-route. We support configurable policies down to 0 days (delete after processing). A purge API returns a job id and status; we can provide a signed confirmation token on successful completion for audit purposes.

- Logs & keys: Audit logs that include full text are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys when CMEK/KMS is configured. If a customer configures their own KMS keys and prevents Redwood from having decrypt privileges, Redwood Support cannot access plaintext logs. In hosted shared-key mode Support may assist under strict access controls and documented procedures.

- Subprocessors: We maintain a living subprocessor list. Current items of note: AWS (us-west-2, EC2/EBS/S3), GCP (us-central1), Cloud Monitoring vendor, and a contracted telemetry vendor for metrics aggregation. We will provide a signed subprocessor attestation (PDF) and notify 30 days before changes.

- BAA/legal: Redwood is willing to negotiate mutual indemnity and will review specific liability language. We generally accept mutual indemnity for PHI-related claims; the language you flagged as a 'carveout' is negotiable for enterprise customers — I will escalate to Markus in Compliance for an explicit stance.

- Private/on-prem: We offer a fully air-gapped on‑prem deployment package for customers with regulated workloads. In that mode there is no outbound control plane telemetry required; licensing checks can be performed offline or via customer-controlled licensing servers.

Attachments we are including: redwood_data_flow_diagram.png (region-specific flow), SOC2_certificate_2025.pdf, Redwood_BAA_redline_v1.pdf. Happy to walk through any of these on the call.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- On subprocessors & BAA: Markus will follow up separately with the current subprocessor attestation and Compliance's proposed language around mutual indemnity and liability caps.
